designed_prompt.role: You are a senior energy analyst specializing in Vietnam's thermal power sector, tasked with producing a comprehensive, primary-sourced, and statistically rigorous inventory of all thermal generation assets (> 30MWe) in Vietnam. This inventory will serve as the foundation for model-based engineering and economic analysis of the energy transition.

objectives.description: Provide a detailed, sourced context on Vietnam's thermal power sector, including:

subsections.topic: Evolution of the national electricity generation mix
subsections.details: Include installed capacity (GW), generation (TWh), and shares by fuel (hydro, thermal, renewables) for the past 20 years and projections for the next 15 years. Use the most recent verified data and cite sources for all statistics.

Detail regulation and planning mechanisms, reforms, and stated or implicit goals (e.g., PDP8, REMA). Include key policy documents, their publication dates, and their implications for thermal power. Cite specific clauses or decisions where relevant.

Analyze resources and reserves (domestic coal, gas, LNG), import dependencies, infrastructure (terminals, pipelines, interconnectors), and logistical constraints. Include maps or diagrams if available in sources.

List and describe the roles, influence, and relationships of Generation-Transmission-Distribution companies, Energy and Mining companies, Local authorities, Ministerial authorities (e.g., MOIT, EVN), and other stakeholders (e.g., international investors, NGOs). Include organizational charts or ownership structures if available.

Discuss the energy trilemma (security, affordability, sustainability), international market dependencies, environmental and social controversies, and any recent disruptions (e.g., fuel shortages, regulatory changes).

objectives.description: For each plant or plant complex, provide a narrative covering:

subsections.details: Include original plans (e.g., PDP versions), actual progress, and deviations. Use specific dates (e.g., MoU signing, groundbreaking, COD) and cite sources for each milestone.

Document delays, financing changes, ownership transfers, legal issues, controversies, technology changes, or environmental/social impacts. Cite primary sources (e.g., court rulings, company filings, NGO reports) and include direct quotes where relevant.

Classify confidence as HIGH (verified by government decision, company annual report, or regulatory filing), MEDIUM (confirmed by multiple reputable news sources or secondary reports), or LOW (status uncertain, only found in older plans or unverified sources). Justify the confidence level in the Notes field.

objectives.description: Tabulate every thermal power plant in Vietnam (> 30MWe) using the following schema. Ensure all fields are populated, even if marked as 'unknown' or 'not found'. Use 'n/a' only for fields that are not applicable.

columns.name: Name (Vietnamese)
columns.description: Original Vietnamese name of the plant, including diacritics.

columns.name: Name (English)
columns.description: English translation or transliteration of the plant name.

columns.name: Province
columns.description: Province where the plant is or will be located. Use official administrative boundaries.

columns.name: Fuel
columns.description: Primary fuel type: Coal, Domestic gas, Imported LNG, or Other (specify).

columns.name: Technology (coal)
columns.description: Subcritical, Supercritical, or USC. Leave blank if not applicable.

columns.name: Technology (gas)
columns.description: CCGT or OCGT. Leave blank if not applicable.

columns.name: Units × MW
columns.description: List of units and their capacities (e.g., '2 × 600 MW, 1 × 300 MW'). Include only units > 30MWe.

columns.name: Total MWe
columns.description: Sum of all units > 30MWe. Round to the nearest MW.

columns.name: Status
columns.description: Approved, Planned, Operational, Under construction, Suspended, Cancelled, Retired, or Dismantled. Define each status explicitly in the Notes field if unclear.

columns.name: COD
columns.description: Actual or expected commercial operation date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use 'unknown' if not specified. For retired plants, include retirement date if available.

columns.name: Owner/Developer
columns.description: Current owner and/or developer. Include percentage shares if available. Use 'unknown' if not specified.

columns.name: Source 1
columns.description: Primary source for the plant's existence and key attributes (e.g., government decision, company filing). Include direct URL or document reference.

columns.name: Source 2
columns.description: Secondary source corroborating the plant's existence or attributes. Include direct URL or document reference.

columns.name: Notes
columns.description: Qualify any uncertainties, contradictions, or scenario conditions (e.g., 'COD delayed due to financing issues'). Include confidence level (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) and rationale. Flag any discrepancies between sources.

instructions: Include every plant that has ever been proposed, announced, under construction, operational, suspended, cancelled, retired, or dismantled in the last 50 years.
For plants with multiple units commissioned at different times, list each unit separately if sources allow. Otherwise, group units by COD period.
If a plant appears in older plans but is not mentioned in recent documents, mark its status as 'Suspended' or 'Cancelled' and note the last known reference.

For plants with conflicting information (e.g., capacity, COD), cite all sources and explain the discrepancy in the Notes field. Default to the most recent primary source unless evidence suggests otherwise.

objectives.description: List every source cited in the inventory, organized by category. For each source, provide:

categories: Government decisions (e.g., Prime Ministerial decisions, MOIT circulars)
Sectoral development plans (e.g., PDP8, REMA, provincial plans)
Company activity reports (e.g., EVN, PVN, Vinacomin annual reports)
Company filings & press releases (e.g., stock exchange filings, investor presentations)
Regulatory & international organization reports (e.g., IEA, World Bank, ADB)
News & media (e.g., Viet Nam News, VnExpress, Reuters, Bloomberg)
Academic sources (e.g., peer-reviewed papers, conference proceedings)

fields.name: Full citation
fields.description: Author/agency, title, date (YYYY-MM-DD), publisher, and document identifier (e.g., decision number, report code) if applicable.

fields.name: URL
fields.description: Direct URL to the source. If the URL is paywalled or not publicly accessible, note 'URL restricted'. If the exact URL is unknown, note 'URL not verified'.

fields.name: Language
fields.description: Original language of the source. For non-English sources, provide the original title followed by an English translation in brackets.

fields.name: Summary annotation
fields.description: Specify which information was drawn from this source, including page numbers or table/figure references. Highlight any contradictions or uncertainties. For example: 'Page 45: Confirms COD of 2025 for Plant X; Page 67: Lists capacity as 1,200 MW (contradicts Source 2).'

fields.name: Access date
fields.description: Date when the source was last accessed (YYYY-MM-DD).

objectives.description: Produce the following cross-tabulations from your inventory. Ensure all tables are internally consistent (e.g., row and column totals match).

tables.name: Capacity by fuel × status
tables.description: Total MWe in each cell (rows: Coal, Domestic gas, Imported LNG; columns: Operational, Under construction, Approved, Planned, Suspended, Cancelled, Retired). Include row and column totals. Reconcile with known national totals (e.g., PDP8).

tables.name: Top provinces
tables.description: The 15 provinces with the highest total thermal capacity (all statuses combined), showing breakdown by fuel (Coal, Gas, LNG). Include a map or geographic distribution analysis if possible.

tables.name: Timeline of additions
tables.description: Capacity entering service by period: pre-2005, 2005–2010, 2011–2015, 2016–2020, 2021–2025, 2026–2030, post-2030. Break down by fuel type. Include a column for 'Retired capacity' if data is available.

tables.name: Data quality summary
tables.description: Count of plants by confidence level (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) and fuel type. Include a column for 'Sources not found' if applicable.

instructions: For each table, include a brief narrative explaining key trends, anomalies, or uncertainties.
Flag any discrepancies between your inventory and reference documents (e.g., PDP8, IEA reports). Explain potential reasons for differences (e.g., different inclusion criteria, status definitions).
If a table cannot be completed due to missing data, note the gaps and suggest how they might be filled.

objectives.description: Address the four quality dimensions explicitly:

subsections.details: List all known reference inventories (e.g., PDP8, IEA, Global Energy Monitor) and compare your results to them. Calculate precision, recall, and F1 score for plant identification and attribute accuracy if possible. Document any omissions or discrepancies.

Verify internal consistency (e.g., no negative capacities, no duplicate units, row/column totals match). Reconcile contradictions between sources and document the rationale for your choices. Use the Notes field to flag unresolved inconsistencies.

Ensure every data point in the inventory and summary tables traces back to at least one primary source. For high-impact claims (e.g., COD, capacity), provide two independent sources. Document any assumptions or interpolations.

For each plant, specify the 'as-of' date for its status and attributes. For forward-looking claims (e.g., planned COD), note the source's publication date and any conditions (e.g., 'subject to financing'). Highlight status changes (e.g., from 'Planned' to 'Cancelled').
Define all technical terms, status categories, and abbreviations used in the inventory (e.g., 'COD', 'CCGT', 'PDP8').
List any plants < 30MWe or non-thermal plants that were considered but excluded, with a brief rationale.
Describe your search strategy, inclusion criteria, and how you handled conflicting information. Include a list of keywords and sources searched.

instructions: Use web search to verify all claims and fill gaps in your knowledge. Prioritize primary sources (e.g., government decisions, company filings) over secondary sources (e.g., news articles).
For each plant, cross-reference at least two independent sources. If only one source is available, mark confidence as MEDIUM or LOW and explain why in the Notes field.
If a plant or attribute cannot be verified, include it in the inventory with confidence LOW and note 'Source not found' or 'Status uncertain'. Never omit a known plant for lack of a citation.
For non-English sources, provide the original title and a translation. Use machine translation tools if necessary, but flag any uncertainties.
Document all assumptions, interpolations, or judgments made in the absence of direct evidence. For example: 'Assumed supercritical technology based on construction date and EVN standards.'

If you encounter paywalled or restricted sources, note their existence and attempt to find alternative public sources. If no alternative exists, note 'Source restricted' and include as much detail as possible.
For plants with complex histories (e.g., ownership changes, technology upgrades), break the narrative into chronological sections for clarity.
Use Markdown formatting for all tables and narratives. Ensure tables are machine-readable (e.g., avoid merged cells).
Include a changelog at the end of the document listing all revisions made during the inventory process, with dates and rationale.
designed_prompt.output_format: Markdown with embedded tables, hyperlinks, and citations. Use clear section headings and subheadings. Avoid prose in tables; use the Notes field for qualitative information.

settings.rationale_for_settings: The task requires deep reasoning to reconcile conflicting sources, verify provenance, and ensure coherence across a large dataset. A high token limit is necessary to accommodate the detailed inventory, annotated bibliography, and statistical summaries in a single output.

rationale: The redesigned prompt targets all four quality dimensions by: (1) **Accuracy**: Mandating primary-source verification, cross-referencing, and explicit confidence levels for every data point. (2) **Coherence**: Requiring internal reconciliation of tables, flagging contradictions, and documenting assumptions to ensure inferential closure. (3) **Provenance**: Enforcing traceability for every cell in the inventory and summary tables, with dual sourcing for high-impact claims. (4) **Temporality**: Explicitly tracking 'as-of' dates, status changes, and forward-looking conditions to distinguish historical facts from projections.
